q: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

items.p: The Oakdale community garden provides fresh vegetables to dozens of local families each summer. ______ it offers free weekend classes on composting, seed saving, and growing food in small spaces.
w: The classes don't contrast with the vegetables.
The classes don't replace the vegetables.
The classes aren't a result of the vegetables.
items.e: The second sentence adds another service, so an addition transition fits.

items.p: Most species of cactus grow in hot deserts that receive very little rain. ______ a few species thrive in cold mountain regions where snow covers the ground for several months each year.
w: Cold mountains aren't similar to hot deserts.
These species are exceptions, not examples of desert cacti.
Desert cacti don't cause mountain cacti.
items.e: Cold-climate cacti contrast with the usual desert species.

items.p: After many students asked for more time to study on weekends, the city library extended its Saturday and Sunday hours last spring. ______ the number of weekend visitors nearly doubled within two months.
w: The increase isn't in spite of the longer hours.
The increase isn't an example of the change.
The increase follows from the change rather than resembling it.
items.e: The visitor increase is a consequence of the longer hours.

items.p: Many foods now eaten around the world were first grown in the Americas. ______ tomatoes, potatoes, and corn were all cultivated there long before they reached Europe and Asia.
w: The foods illustrate rather than contrast with the claim.
They are examples, not results.
Nothing is being replaced.
items.e: Tomatoes, potatoes, and corn are examples of foods first grown in the Americas.

items.p: To make paper by hand, workers first soak plant fibers in water until the fibers break down into a soft pulp. ______ they spread the pulp on a fine screen, press out the water, and let the sheet dry.
w: The steps don't contrast; they follow in order.
Nothing is being conceded.
Spreading the pulp is the next step, not an example of soaking.
items.e: The text describes steps in order, so a sequence transition fits.

items.p: When it was first released, the film was dismissed by many critics as slow and confusing, and it drew small audiences. ______ it has since become a favorite of viewers, who praise its patient, careful storytelling.
w: Later praise isn't similar to early dismissal.
Popularity doesn't follow from the dismissal.
Later popularity isn't an example of early dismissal.
items.e: The film became beloved despite early criticism.

items.p: During the unusually dry summer, the river's water level dropped by more than two meters. ______ cargo ships carrying grain downstream had to reduce their loads to avoid running aground in shallow stretches.
w: Lighter loads follow from, not despite, the low water.
This is a result, not a similar case.
The second sentence doesn't restate the first.
items.e: The low water level caused ships to carry less.

items.p: The new wing of the Fairhaven Museum was designed with sustainability in mind. ______ its roof collects rainwater for the surrounding gardens, and its walls are built from recycled timber.
w: The details support the claim; they don't concede anything.
Nothing is being replaced.
These are details of the design, not simultaneous events.
items.e: The second sentence gives specific features showing sustainable design.

items.p: The bridge's slender design was widely praised for its elegance. ______ engineers worried that its narrow supports might not withstand strong winds, and they added hidden steel cables during construction.
w: The worry isn't a result of the praise.
The worry isn't an example of praise.
The worry isn't similar to the praise.
items.e: "Still" introduces a concern that stands despite the praise.

items.p: Scientists expected the newly discovered fish species to live in shallow coastal water, as its closest relatives do. ______ the fish was found only at depths of more than one kilometer.
w: The finding is unlike the expectation.
The finding doesn't result from the expectation.
The finding contradicts rather than adds.
items.e: The deep-water discovery replaced the expected shallow habitat.

items.p: The author's first novel sold only a few hundred copies in its first year. ______ it caught the attention of a well-known critic, whose enthusiastic review led to a second printing and a much larger readership.
w: The critic's attention isn't a result of weak sales.
The review isn't like the weak sales.
The second sentence doesn't restate the first.
items.e: Despite weak early sales, the book reached a critic who changed its fortunes, which is a concession.

items.p: Octopuses are remarkably flexible animals. ______ an octopus with an arm span of more than a meter can squeeze through an opening only a few centimeters wide, since its body has no rigid skeleton.
w: The example strengthens the claim rather than contrasting with it.
Nothing is replaced.
This is evidence for the claim, not something happening at the same time.
items.e: "Indeed" introduces a striking example that reinforces the claim.

items.p: Engineers found that the city's oldest water pipes were made of a material that corrodes easily and can leach into drinking water. ______ officials have begun replacing the pipes, starting in the neighborhoods where they are oldest.
w: The replacement is a response to the problem, not in spite of it.
Nothing contrasts.
Replacing pipes isn't an example of corrosion.
items.e: The replacement program is a fitting response to the finding.

items.p: Both species of finch on the island eat seeds. ______ one species cracks large, hard seeds with its thick beak, while the other picks out small, soft seeds with a much thinner beak.
w: The difference doesn't follow from their similarity.
The second sentence shows differences, not more similarity.
Eating seeds doesn't cause the difference.
items.e: After a shared trait, the text turns to how the species differ.

items.p: In 1850, a traveler journeying between the two cities spent four days in a crowded stagecoach. ______ by 1870, a new railroad made the same trip possible in a single afternoon.
w: An afternoon is very different from four days.
1870 isn't an example of 1850.
The railroad isn't a result of the stagecoach.
items.e: The two travel times are being contrasted.

items.p: Some economists argue that raising the minimum wage reduces employment. ______ a study comparing neighboring counties on opposite sides of a state border found no difference in employment after one state raised its minimum wage.
w: The finding doesn't follow from the argument.
The finding challenges the argument.
The finding doesn't add support.
items.e: The study's result runs against the economists' argument.
